sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the phrase "Your pious ones will bless You" means they draw down a revelation into Malchus specifically from the level of Ein Sof that is beyond comprehension, where only acknowledgment (Hoda'ah) applies.

translations.translation: And this will be understood by prefacing what is said
"All Your works shall praise You, and Your pious ones will bless You,"
and it is brought in the Zohar
that the explanation of "will bless You" (yevarchuchah) is "they will bless *koh*."
And the Rebbe
(the Rebbe Rashab)
of blessed memory
(in his maamar beginning "Padeh b'Shalom" from the year 5668),
explains that *koh* is Malchus,
and "they will bless *koh*" means to draw down a revelation of light into Malchus.
And it is stated "and Your pious ones will bless You,"
that this drawing down is specifically through the power of "Your pious ones."
And the explanation is,
that this matter of "Your pious ones will bless You" is in proximity and continuation to "All Your works shall praise You,"
that is,
because the drawing down into Malchus
(which is through "Your pious ones")
is from a very exalted place
(the Ein Sof that is above the chain of descent)
regarding which comprehension does not apply, only acknowledgment (Hoda'ah) alone,
"they will praise You."
And the drawing down from there
(in the manner of blessing)
is specifically through the power of "Your pious ones."

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section distinguishes between prayer (from below to above, requesting new light) and blessing (from above to below, commanding an existing flow), noting that prayer can draw a new will from Ein Sof while blessing is a certain command.

translations.translation: And in order to understand the great superiority of the drawing down in the manner of blessing from the place where there is acknowledgment (Hoda'ah),
the maamar prefaces the distinction between blessing and prayer,
that in each one there is an advantage over the other.
And the explanation is,
that prayer is from below to above,
meaning that the one praying is below and requests that they bestow upon him from above,
and blessing is from above to below,
that the one who blesses is above the source from which the blessing is drawn, and he draws it from above to below.
And this is that blessing is in the manner of a command,
for since the one who blesses is above the source from which the blessing is drawn,
therefore he has the power to command.
And this is that blessing is specifically for one who has the power to bless
(like Avraham Avinu, to whom the Holy One, blessed be He, said "the blessings are given to you"),
[and unlike prayer, which anyone can pray,
and moreover, everyone is commanded to pray],
because in order to bless,
the one who blesses must be above the source from which the blessing is drawn.
And from this the advantage of blessing over prayer is understood,
for in prayer,
which is a request that they draw down the influence,
there is no certainty that the request will be fulfilled.
But in blessing, which is in the manner of a command—the influence will certainly be drawn down,
since the one who blesses has the power to command.
And the advantage of prayer over blessing is in the drawing down itself,
that the drawing down through prayer is more exalted.
For the matter of blessing is to draw down what already exists in the source, and not something new,
and the matter of prayer is a request from the Holy One, blessed be He, that even if the influence is not changed even in the source, heaven forbid,
and moreover, even if it has been decreed upon him that he should be ill, heaven forbid, and the like,
nevertheless,
a new influence will be drawn down to him from the Ein Sof that is above the chain of descent.
For this is what is said in several prayers, "May it be His will" (Yehi Ratzon),
that the explanation of "May it be His will" is that there should be a new will.
And the reason for this, that the drawing down of a new light is specifically through prayer,
is "for You desire the work of Your hands,"
and therefore,
through prayer,
the work of the one below,
they reach the Ein Sof that is above the chain of descent.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the blessing of the pious ones combines both advantages: it draws a new will from Ein Sof (like prayer) yet is issued as a command (like blessing), as seen in the Jerusalem Talmud about a righteous person's decree overriding G-d's.

translations.translation: And based on this, the great superiority of the blessing
(of "Your pious ones")
is understood, that its drawing down is from the place where there is acknowledgment (Hoda'ah),
for in this blessing there are both advantages.
That the drawing down is from the Ein Sof that is above the chain of descent,
meaning that through this blessing a new will is made—the advantage of prayer.
And nevertheless it is
(not prayer,
a request,
but rather)
a blessing,
in the manner of a command.
And this is similar to what is brought in the Jerusalem Talmud
on the verse
"And you shall decree a thing, and it will be established for you,"
that even if He
(the Holy One, blessed be He)
says "thus" and you say "thus,"
yours stands and Mine does not stand.
For this, that the Holy One, blessed be He, nullifies His decree because of the decree of the righteous person,
is
because the righteous person draws down a new will—the advantage of prayer,
and the manner of the nullification of the decree is
(not through a request,
but rather)
through the decree of the righteous person—the advantage of blessing, which is in the manner of a command.
